newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitians go to polls in local elections.
newsitem.headline: Haitians go to polls in local elections.

text.p: Haitians began voting on Sunday in senate and local elections against a background of discontent against President Rene Preval's government.
Analysts expect a low-turnout and only a trickle of people turned up to cast votes as polls opened, with more people intent on going to Sunday mass.

The elections are the fifth since parliamentary elections in June 1995, held after a U.S.-led military intervention ousted a military regime and restored former president Jean Bertrand Aristide to power in October 1994.
But many Haitians have expressed frustration that the present government has done little to alleviate the country's appalling poverty, draining enthusiasm for the democratic process.

At stake are nine seats in the Senate, two parliamentary seats, 133 town delegations and 565 district assemblies. They will bring democratic rule to a local level for the first time in the country's history. More than 4,028,000 Haitains are registered to vote.
